Find the value of $\frac{2}{3}÷\frac{5}{7}$ given the model above.
question.worked_solution:
The denominators are $3$ and $7.$ We can make a common denominator of $3\times 7=21.$ 

We split the shape on the left of the division sign into $7$ parts vertically, and we split the shape on the right into $3$ parts horizontally:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14153326/assets/d9fdbf9a9f569024446f1be9866d51d32cd77dd69868b6efc30b16a7266abb50.png)

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{14}{21}÷\frac{15}{21}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
14÷15=\frac{14}{15}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{2}{3}÷\frac{5}{7}=\frac{14}{15}.
$$
